title: Building the Intelligence Profile: Meridian Financial — Complete
introduction: An intelligence profile is the written output of the passive reconnaissance phase. It is not a list of tool outputs — it is a structured document that answers the question: 'What do we know about this target, and what does it mean for the engagement?' This block walks through the complete Meridian Financial intelligence profile — showing how everything found across Missions 1–4 connects into one coherent picture.

sections.heading: Section 1: Asset inventory
sections.content:
The asset inventory lists every domain, subdomain, and IP address attributed to the target. It is built progressively during the reconnaissance phase and updated as new assets are discovered.

**Meridian Financial — Confirmed Assets:**

Domains (in scope, verified via WHOIS):
— meridian-financial.com (primary domain, registered 2009, GoDaddy, Cloudflare NS)

Subdomains discovered (DNS enumeration + Certificate Transparency):
— www.meridian-financial.com → Cloudflare IP (CDN-protected)
— portal.meridian-financial.com → CNAME to meridian-portal.force.com (Salesforce)
— dev.meridian-financial.com → 45.77.180.10 (Vultr VPS, direct IP, no CDN)
— legacy.meridian-financial.com → 45.77.180.11 (Vultr VPS, direct IP, no CDN)
— mail.meridian-financial.com → Cloudflare IP (purpose unclear — not the MX server)

IP addresses identified:
— Cloudflare IP range (main site, mail subdomain) — CDN-proxied, real origin unknown
— 45.77.180.10 — dev server, Vultr, direct
— 45.77.180.11 — legacy server, Vultr, direct

Note: meridianfinancial.com (no hyphen) — third-party registration identified in Mission 2. Active phishing infrastructure, not client-owned. Reported as out-of-band advisory finding.

callout.title: The asset inventory is dynamic
callout.content: The asset inventory starts with what is in the scope document. It grows during DNS enumeration (subdomains) and search engine reconnaissance (additional infrastructure). Every new asset is checked against the scope document. In-scope discoveries go into the investigation queue. Out-of-scope discoveries go into a separate 'noted but not investigated' section. The final asset inventory in the report lists both — with clear labelling.

sections.heading: Section 2: Infrastructure architecture
sections.content:
The infrastructure architecture section describes how the organisation's internet presence is structured — the relationships between assets, providers, and services.

**Meridian Financial — Infrastructure Picture:**

**DNS and CDN layer**: DNS managed through Cloudflare (confirmed via NS records). Main website behind Cloudflare CDN. CDN origin IP unknown — Cloudflare protects it. Two subdomains (dev and legacy) resolve to direct IPs not behind Cloudflare — representing the CDN gap in their architecture.

**Email infrastructure**: Google Workspace (confirmed MX records: aspmx.l.google.com, priority 1). SPF authorises Google. No backup MX — single mail provider with no failover.

**Application platforms**: Main application — framework unclear (behind CDN, needs active testing). Customer portal — Salesforce Force.com (confirmed via CNAME and three independent TXT tokens). CRM platform — Salesforce (confirmed via TXT verification token and SPF include).

**Hosting**: Primary infrastructure on Cloudflare-proxied servers (provider unknown). Development and legacy servers on Vultr VPS (lower-cost VPS provider — common for dev environments, less common for production). Two VPS servers in the same IP range suggests they were provisioned together.

**Architecture gap**: The primary website, the customer portal, and email are all behind CDN or managed cloud services (Google, Salesforce). The development and legacy subdomains are on VPS hosting without CDN — a common pattern where the main service was migrated to a CDN-protected infrastructure but the older servers were not decommissioned.

callout.title: The architecture picture guides active testing planning
callout.content: The architecture gap — CDN-protected main site vs direct-IP dev and legacy servers — is the most operationally significant finding from the infrastructure analysis. It tells the testing team that the main site requires different testing approaches than the development servers. The dev and legacy servers can be reached directly, scanned directly, and tested directly. The main site's scanning must account for the Cloudflare layer — which may block or rate-limit certain scan types.

sections.heading: Section 3: Technology stack
sections.content:
The technology stack section consolidates every technology disclosure from passive reconnaissance.

**Meridian Financial — Known Technology Stack (passive recon only):**

Email: Google Workspace (confirmed MX)
CRM/Sales: Salesforce (confirmed TXT token, portal CNAME, SPF include — three independent sources)
DNS management: Cloudflare
CDN: Cloudflare
Development hosting: Vultr (two VPS servers)
Customer portal hosting: Salesforce Force.com
Software versioning: unknown (active testing required)
Web application framework: unknown (active testing required)
Database platform: unknown (backup file found but not opened)

**Intelligence from document metadata (passive):**
One PDF found via Google Dorking contained metadata: Author field — 'Sarah Mitchell', Organisation — 'Meridian Financial IT Security', Software — 'Microsoft Word 2019'. This confirms: an employee named Sarah Mitchell works in IT Security, the organisation uses Microsoft Office (suggesting potential Microsoft 365 productivity suite — worth checking in DNS; existing SPF record only shows Google so Office is not confirmed for email), and the document was created in the 2019-2022 era.

**Intelligence from job postings (passive):**
A LinkedIn job posting for 'Senior Cloud Infrastructure Engineer' referenced AWS and Terraform. This suggests the organisation is building or expanding AWS infrastructure — not yet confirmed in DNS but worth investigating during active testing.

callout.title: Multi-source technology confirmation
callout.content: Salesforce was confirmed by three independent passive sources: the portal.meridian-financial.com CNAME pointing to force.com, a TXT record containing an SF_domain_auth token, and an SPF include:_spf.salesforce.com entry. Three independent sources mean this is established fact — it goes in the report as confirmed, not as a hypothesis. Single-source technology identifications (like the AWS job posting) go in the report as 'intelligence suggesting' — requiring active-phase confirmation.

sections.heading: Section 4: Email security posture
sections.content:
Email security posture is a distinct intelligence section because it directly informs a common attack path: phishing. The email security posture tells the team whether the domain can be used to spoof phishing emails against the client's staff or customers.

**Meridian Financial — Email Security Posture:**

SPF (Sender Policy Framework): v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all
— Authorised senders: Google Workspace only
— Enforcement: ~all (SoftFail) — unauthorised senders are flagged but not rejected
— Intelligence: only Google is authorised; Salesforce is NOT in the SPF (they may send email from Salesforce but it is not in the SPF record — potential for Salesforce-origin phishing)

DMARC: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@meridian-financial.com
— Policy: p=none (monitoring only)
— Implication: emails failing both SPF and DKIM are DELIVERED to recipients. The domain can be spoofed in phishing campaigns. An attacker who sends a phishing email appearing to come from security@meridian-financial.com will have it delivered to any recipient whose email provider relies on DMARC policy.
— Severity: HIGH. This is a finding that enables social engineering attacks against the client's staff and customers.

DKIM: not confirmed in passive reconnaissance (requires active DNS testing of selector records — confirm authorisation in RoE)

**Finding**: The combination of p=none DMARC and ~all SPF enforcement means this domain is spoofable. Recommended action: implement DMARC p=quarantine as an immediate step, with a roadmap to p=reject within 90 days.

sections.heading: Section 5: Critical findings from search engine reconnaissance
sections.content:
The Google Dorking phase produced four critical/high findings that are documented here as standalone findings with full evidence chains.

**Finding 1 — Critical: Unauthenticated production API (resolved during engagement)**
URL: meridian-financial.com/api/v1/internal
Discovery method: robots.txt review — Disallow: /api/v1/internal → direct URL access
Evidence: JSON response returning {'status': 'ok', 'version': '2.1.4', 'environment': 'production', 'users': 14329, 'pending_reviews': 47} — no authentication required
Severity: CRITICAL — live production data accessible without authentication
Status: Remediated during engagement. Client notified day 4, 15:30 UTC. Endpoint returned 404 by day 4, 19:30 UTC.

**Finding 2 — Critical: Open directory with production backup files**
URL: meridian-financial.com/backup/
Discovery method: Google Dork — site:meridian-financial.com intitle:"index of"
Evidence: Directory listing enabled — files visible: database_backup_2024-07-01.sql.gz (2.4MB), config_backup_prod.tar.gz (847KB), apache_logs_june.zip (12MB). Last modified: 8 days prior to discovery.
Severity: CRITICAL — production database backup publicly accessible
Action: Not downloaded. URL and directory contents documented by screenshot only.

**Finding 3 — High: Admin portal publicly indexed**
URL: meridian-financial.com/admin/login
Discovery method: Google Dork — site:meridian-financial.com inurl:admin
Evidence: Login page loads without authentication challenge. Page title: 'Meridian Admin Portal — Internal Use Only'. Software version not visible on login page (requires active testing).
Severity: HIGH — admin portal publicly accessible and indexed. Active testing of this portal is in-scope; to be addressed in active testing phase.

**Finding 4 — High: Internal HR document indexed by Google**
URL: meridian-financial.com/documents/HR_Employee_Handbook_2023_DRAFT.pdf
Discovery method: Google Dork — site:meridian-financial.com filetype:pdf
Evidence: Document visible in Google search results. Accessible via direct URL. Not downloaded — URL and Google result screenshot only.
Severity: HIGH — internal HR document (DRAFT) publicly accessible and indexed. Contains employee policies potentially useful for social engineering preparation.

keyTerms.definition: The structured written output of the passive reconnaissance phase. Organises all findings into: asset inventory, infrastructure architecture, technology stack, email security posture, and critical findings. The document that is delivered before active testing begins.

The pattern where an organisation's main infrastructure is behind CDN protection but development, staging, or legacy servers are not. The gap represents direct-IP assets that are reachable without CDN filtering.

An SPF record enforcement level that marks emails from unauthorised senders as suspicious but allows delivery. Weaker than HardFail (-all) which rejects unauthorised senders. Often combined with a p=none DMARC policy — producing a domain that is effectively spoofable.
